item.p: Layout (bindings/javascript/, glossary , ): the shim sxml_javascript.c (with its interface sxml_javascript.h, not a public header) uses only the public API, as the CLI does. It builds as a library in every preset, so -Werror, clang-tidy and ast-grep see it (cmake/SxmlLint.cmake globs bindings/); under WASI it links into sxml.wasm, a reactor module (-mexec-model=reactor, export_name, --strip-all). The package is hand-written TypeScript (src/index.ts, src/wasi.ts), erasable syntax only, so Node.js (22.18 and later) runs it and its tests directly; tsc 5.9.3, a devDependency, type-checks (ctest javascript/typecheck after npm ci there) and builds dist/. No runtime dependencies.

WASI: the module imports only clock_time_get, fd_write, fd_close and fd_seek (sxml does no I/O; resources come through the resolver). The package supplies these itself in Node.js and browsers alike (real clocks; EBADF; ENOSYS for any other import), instead of node:wasi and a browser polyfill: one code path. So 's fast-call workaround does not concern the package; tools/run-wasi.mjs is unchanged. Checked in headless Chromium (fetch, resolver, clock).

API: load() gives an Sxml; createProcessor({resolver}); Processor.parse, compile (an XPathExpression with named external variables, item()*, NCName or Q{uri}local), evaluate, value, serialize, dispose; Value.serialize, toString (adaptive), dispose; failures throw SxmlError (status, code prefix:local, description, line, column). JavaScript data becomes XDM as fn:parse-json reads its JSON (a string is an xs:string), one general rule instead of per-type conversions; serialization options are fn:serialize's options map, read by sxml_serialization_parameter_reader (camelCase keys accepted). The resolver is a synchronous callback (sxml_host.resolve import) returning a string, bytes or nothing; an exception it throws is rethrown; it must not use its processor. XQuery arrives additively once xquery.h is implemented: a Processor.compileQuery() giving an expression object with the same evaluate and the query's serialization parameters as the default of serialize; resource kinds already include xquery-module.

Memory: every package object owning C memory is a handle (glossary); dispose() releases it, a FinalizationRegistry releases what is never disposed. A processor's destruction releases its live values and expressions first, since they cannot outlive it in C. Each processor has a counting allocator: tests check that destruction leaves 0 allocations and run the allocation-failure loop () from JavaScript.

Size budget (, glossary ): at this commit the sxml CLI module is 1,820,106 bytes stripped, 629,585 gzipped (zlib -9); sxml.wasm 1,788,836 and 617,898. Phase 2 grew both past 's 1.5 MB and 450 KB (from 1,213,261 and 358,020); -flto -Oz saves 2%, so the growth is code and tables, not flags. The budget becomes 2,000,000 bytes stripped and 700,000 gzipped for both modules, checked by ctest javascript/size_budget (wasm preset), which prints the sizes. The owner may instead want optional parts as separate modules (PLAN.md, risks): see "Proposed".
npm name: sxml is taken on npm (another project, 1.0.4); the package is sxml-js until the owner chooses.

Release 0.2.0: SXML_VERSION_* 0.2.0, equal to SXML_API_VERSION; CMake project version 0.2.0; CHANGELOG.md; docs/RELEASE.md says how to cut a release. From 0.2.0 the public headers are stable (): a release adds declarations (minor before 1.0.0) and never changes one without a major (before 1.0.0, minor) version and a record. Tagging and publishing to npm are the owner's.
